CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · 19 SAFETY CARDS

Staying Safe.

HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Nineteen rules, rehearsed until they are reflexes.

Every card in this class is one safety rule YOU can own: buckle up, hold hands near roads, red means stop, cross on the zebra, stop-look-listen, stop at the edge, walking feet, wear a helmet, give dogs space, don’t touch, hot things, medicine is not candy, fire safety, stop-drop-roll, and the helping spine — stop, ask, tell — with ask-for-help, if-you’re-lost, stay-with-your-group and tell-if-you’re-hurt finishing the set. Each card is right here: the card itself, the rule it prints and one way to practise it today.

One card a sitting is plenty — the whole class is a term of five-minute safety talks, and the order runs road first, home second, fire third and people last. Safety is the one subject where rehearsal is the lesson: a rule you say at a calm curb is the rule that plays back at a busy one. Nothing here is scary. Everything here is said the way the cards say it — plainly, warmly, and with a grown-up’s hand somewhere in the picture.

WHY REHEARSAL WINS

A rule practised calmly is a rule that holds.

Safety teachers agree on the method: name the rule, act it out, and repeat it in the real place — the curb, the car, the kitchen. Fear teaches nothing; a drilled routine teaches everything. That is why this class runs on tiny repetitions done cheerfully, one card a week if that is the pace you and your grown-up choose, and why every page ends in something to DO, not just something to know.

The deck’s quiet center is the Safety Hero card: STOP, ASK, TELL. Every other rule in the set hangs off that spine — stop before the street, ask before touching, tell when something is wrong. If you keep only three words from this class, those are the three, and the card to hang on the fridge is Safety Hero.

THE ROAD SHELF · CARS, CROSSINGS AND BIKES

Out and about: the road shelf.

Nine cards for every walk, ride and drive: buckle up before the wheels turn, hold hands near roads, read the traffic lights, cross on the zebra, stop-look-listen at the curb, stop at the edge, keep your walking feet on the sidewalk, wear a helmet on wheels, and give every dog its space. All right here on this page!

THE HOME SHELF · HOT, PLUGGED-IN, MEDICINE

Indoors: the home shelf.

Three cards for the house: sockets and plugs are don’t-touch, steam and stoves are hot things, and medicine is not candy — the grown-up hands it over, nobody else. All right here on this page!

Don’t TouchHot ThingsMedicine Is Not Candy
THE FIRE SHELF · KNOW IT, DRILL IT

Fire: know it, drill it.

Two cards that rehearse the scary minute so nobody meets it cold: fire safety (notice it, get out, tell a grown-up) and the stop-drop-roll drill every four-year-old can own. All right here on this page!

Fire SafetyStop, Drop, Roll
THE HELPING SHELF · PEOPLE WHO KEEP YOU SAFE

People: the helping shelf.

Five cards for the moments that need another person: the safety-hero spine (stop, ask, tell), asking for help from a trusted grown-up, what to do if you’re lost, staying with your group, and telling someone when you’re hurt. All right here on this page!

Safety HeroAsk for HelpIf You’re LostStay with Your GroupTell If You’re Hurt
AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where this class fits.

Back to the Learning Path ↗Class 32 · Life Skills & Good Habits ↗Class 33 · Community Helpers & Our Neighborhood ↗Class 24 · Transportation & Vehicles ↗First Glance · the Staying-safe sheet ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 19 cards to print ↗

Class 32 builds the everyday habits this class keeps safe, Class 33 names the helpers a four-year-old can call on — firefighters, police officers, crossing guards — and Class 24 spots the vehicles whose rules this class rehearses. The First Glance safety sheet holds the same words as pictures, ready for the youngest sibling. And when the cards need printing, parents will find the whole deck on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library — download and print buttons under every card, no extra pages to hop through.

Age ranges are a guide, not a test. Start with the rules your week already meets — the car, the curb, the kitchen — and let the card pages do the rehearsing with you.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 1 OF 19

Buckle Up

The car seat rule that never takes a day off: the strap goes on before the wheels turn, every ride, near and far. On this card the buckle clicks and the boy grins — because being strapped in is YOUR first job as a big-kid passenger.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Safe in the car” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Next car ride, take the job: check that every belt in the back seat is clicked before the driver turns the key. The buckle click becomes the ride’s starting bell — and it is yours.

Keep going

Buckle Up is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Hold Hands Near Roads.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 2 OF 19

Hold Hands Near Roads

Your hand in your grown-up’s hand, from the door to the door. The card shows the whole deal: fingers locked, crossing while the car waits — because your grip on a grown-up is the safest strap there is.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“A grown-up hand and a small hand, all the way” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Walk to the mailbox and back with the one rule said out loud: near a road, hands lock. Be the one who reminds YOUR grown-up — the day you enforce it, the rule is yours.

Keep going

Hold Hands Near Roads is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Traffic Lights.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 3 OF 19

Traffic Lights

The street speaks in colors, and this card teaches the two that matter first: red means YOU stop, green means go — when the road is safe for you to cross. The smiling light on the card makes the colors easy to love and easier to remember.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Red = stop · green = go when safe” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Stand at one light and call the colors together: red — feet stop, green — eyes check, then go. Three lights is a full lesson; the yellow can wait for a later class.

Keep going

Traffic Lights is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Zebra Crossing.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 4 OF 19

Zebra Crossing

The striped road where walkers win. This card shows the crossing sign and the stripes themselves — the one place YOU step out proudly, after a stop and a look both ways.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Cross safely” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Cross on the stripes today and lead the ritual yourself: stop at the edge, look both ways, walk straight across the stripes — no diagonals.

Keep going

Zebra Crossing is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Stop, Look, Listen.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 5 OF 19

Stop, Look, Listen

The three-step curb drill, one card, three signs: STOP at the edge, LOOK left and right, LISTEN for engines before a toe moves. Drill it calmly on quiet walks and it plays back on the busy ones — your feet will already know it.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Stop · Look · Listen” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Play the three words at any quiet curb: your grown-up says stop, YOU look left and right and cup your ear. Then swap roles so you get to be the caller too.

Keep going

Stop, Look, Listen is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Stop at the Edge.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 6 OF 19

Stop at the Edge

The curb is a cliff to a ball, a scooter and a running four-year-old. The card’s hero plants his palm out at the edge — the same stop YOU practise at every sidewalk, parking lot and driveway.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Feet behind the line, every time” — printed on the card.

Try it today

At the next curb, practise the plant: both feet stop a giant step back from the edge, palm out. Ball rolls to the street? It waits there — the grown-up is the fetcher, not you.

Keep going

Stop at the Edge is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Walk, Don’t Run.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 7 OF 19

Walk, Don’t Run

Near the street, walking feet. The card says it with pictures: one boy strolling while his sneaker pals dash past — the running belongs on YOUR grass and playgrounds, and the walking belongs where cars go.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Walking feet near the street” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Choose a stretch of sidewalk and make it the walking challenge: who can pass it with the calmest feet — you or your grown-up? Running waits for the park at the end.

Keep going

Walk, Don’t Run is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Wear a Helmet.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 8 OF 19

Wear a Helmet

Wheels on, helmet on — scooters, bikes, trikes, all of it. The card’s rider gives a thumbs-up from under a purple helmet because that is the whole argument: YOUR helmet is what lets the ride be fun.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Protect your head” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Pick the helmet together and let the sticker or color be YOUR choice — a helmet you picked is a helmet you wear. The rule stays: no helmet, no wheels.

Keep going

Wear a Helmet is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Safe Distance.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 9 OF 19

Safe Distance

Dogs are family to their people and strangers to everybody else — so the card teaches the space: give the dog room, keep your hand to yourself until the owner says yes to YOU. Kind for the dog, safe for you.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Give space · ask before touching” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Meet a leashed dog on a walk and run the sequence: stop, ask the owner, wait for the yes. A no is a fine answer too — wave hello with your hand instead.

Keep going

Safe Distance is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Don’t Touch.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 10 OF 19

Don’t Touch

Sockets, plugs, wires and the cleaning shelf: the big red hand on this card covers them all. The rule under the picture is the useful half — don’t touch, and then what YOU do instead: ask a grown-up.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Ask a grown-up” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Tour one room and play red-hand detective: point at everything a hand must not touch — sockets, cords, the cleaning shelf — and say the words: don’t touch, ask a grown-up.

Keep going

Don’t Touch is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Hot Things.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 11 OF 19

Hot Things

Steam is the warning sign a four-year-old can read: the mug, the kettle, the stove top. The card’s red hand says don’t touch, and the yellow banner underneath gives the safe move YOU can make — ask a grown-up.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Steam, stoves and kettles — look, don’t touch” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Kitchen tour, steam edition: find the kettle, the stove, the oven and the mug, and show your grown-up the steam from a safe step back. Steam means stop.

Keep going

Hot Things is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Medicine Is Not Candy.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 12 OF 19

Medicine Is Not Candy

The bottle on this card frowns for a reason: pills and gummies look sweet and are not. The rule is one breath long — medicine is not candy, ask first — and a grown-up is the only hand that opens the bottle. Never yours.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Ask first — only a grown-up hands it over” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Say the rule at vitamin time and mean it: vitamins are medicine too, so the grown-up hands them over — never you. If you ever find a bottle, don’t touch: call your grown-up.

Keep going

Medicine Is Not Candy is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Fire Safety.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 13 OF 19

Fire Safety

The fire plan in three calm moves: notice it, get out, tell a grown-up — with the smoke alarm on the card teaching YOU the sound before any real alarm sounds. Rehearsed twice, it holds for life.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Notice it → get out → tell a grown-up” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Find the smoke alarm’s home and press its test button with a grown-up — the beep is loud, and loud is the point. Then walk the exit route from YOUR bedroom to the front door once, slowly.

Keep going

Fire Safety is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Stop, Drop, Roll.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 14 OF 19

Stop, Drop, Roll

If YOUR clothes ever catch, the body already knows: STOP where you are, DROP to the ground, ROLL over the flames until they are out. Three steps, one drill, practised laughing on the living-room rug — that is exactly how it should go in.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“The three steps every kid knows” — printed on the card.

Try it today

On a rug or the grass, drill the three steps with giggles: stop, drop, roll — three rolls, then up. Practised as a game, the move lives in YOUR body if it is ever needed.

Keep going

Stop, Drop, Roll is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Safety Hero.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 15 OF 19

Safety Hero

The spine of the whole class on one card: STOP when something feels wrong to YOU, ASK a grown-up you trust, TELL what happened. The caped hero on the card makes the rules feel like a superpower — because they are one.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Stop · Ask · Tell” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Make the three words your family’s secret code this week: stop, ask, tell. When your grown-up calls one at random across the day, answer with the move and the words.

Keep going

Safety Hero is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Ask for Help.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 16 OF 19

Ask for Help

Needing help is not being small — it is the hero move this card shows: a hand up high, a grown-up thumbs-up back. The badge underneath names the target: a TRUSTED grown-up. Can you name two or three? Naming them is the practice.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Tell a trusted grown-up” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Name your trusted grown-ups out loud: two at home, one or two at school or with the neighbors. Rehearse the sentence — “I need help, please” — until it comes out easy.

Keep going

Ask for Help is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: If You’re Lost.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 17 OF 19

If You’re Lost

Lost has a script, and this card is it: STAY HERE where you were last seen, FIND a trusted grown-up — a parent, a worker with a name tag, a person with children — and SAY YOUR NAME out loud. Three lines: rehearse them on errands and they are yours forever.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Stay here · find a trusted grown-up · say your name” — printed on the card.

Try it today

On the next errand, pick the lost-spot together: the checkout counter, the information desk, a worker with a name tag. Then rehearse the three lines — stay here, find a trusted grown-up, say my name — with YOUR full name said proud and loud.

Keep going

If You’re Lost is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Stay with Your Group.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 18 OF 19

Stay with Your Group

The line on this card is the whole lesson: nobody wanders, everybody walks with the grown-up. Stay with YOUR group and every outing stays easy — the red stop hand catches the one who drifted.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“Stay together · follow your grown-up” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Next family walk or party, take the job of group checker: count the people before you leave and when you arrive. The job makes the rule stick — and the job is yours.

Keep going

Stay with Your Group is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Tell If You’re Hurt.

STAYING SAFE · CLASS 39 · AGES 4–5 · CARD 19 OF 19

Tell If You’re Hurt

A hurt that is told gets a bandage; a hurt that is hidden gets worse. The card shows the tell: a boy with a scraped knee waving his grown-up over — and the banner puts the rule in words YOU can own.

Download the card ↓

Teaching tips

The card says

“A hurt that is told gets help” — printed on the card.

Try it today

Learn the report: where it hurts, how it happened, and show the spot. Practise on a stuffed animal first — YOU play the grown-up, and the bear reports its sore paw.

Keep going

Tell If You’re Hurt is one of the nineteen rules in Class 39 · Staying Safe — the class page holds the whole set, one shelf per part of life. Next up: Buckle Up.
